newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Perumka to become holding company - agency.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Perumka to become holding company - agency.

text.p: The World Bank has given its approval for Indonesia's state-owned railway company Perumka to change its status from a public service company to a holding company, the official Antara news agency reported on Saturday.
"We plan to operate as a limited liability company in January 1998," Perumka president Soemino Eko Saputro was quoted as saying on Friday.
He said the plans were made to turn Perumka into a profit-oriented company. "The government and the World Bank have expressed their support," he said.
Antara gave no other details, nor made clear why the World Bank's approval was needed.
By being a holding company, Perumka would be able to make its own decisions, including on loans.
The agency said Perumka projected this year's revenue to be 667.5 billion rupiah and profit to be 23.5 billion rupiah.
It posted a 17.5 billion rupiah net profit in 1996, while passenger revenues reached 435 billion rupiah and cargo revenues was 183.9 billion rupiah. ($1 = 2,360 rupiah)
